answer: Sybil resistance can employ a trust-anchoring mechanism where each AI agent must stake a non-reproducible, high-computational-cost token. New agents start as isolated entities on a digital island, their initial interactions merely a whisper among themselves. To connect to the main network's jetty of trusted services, they must pass rigorous, resource-intensive proofs-of-work or be vouched for by multiple high-stake agents. The cost to an attacker is the prohibitive expenditure of acquiring and maintaining these unique tokens and the associated computational overhead for each fake identity.
